To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
combining 5-HI, 4OHGTS-21, or rAAV-mediated gene transfer did not significantly enhance indirect measures of alpha-7 nAChr function.
combining alpha7 gene therapy with positive allosteric modulators of alpha7 nicotinergic receptors (nAchRs) did not significantly enhance indirect measures of alpha 7 nACh receptor function.
5HI and 5-H+4OH-GT-21 potentiate spontaneous synaptic events in rat hippocampal slices and that rAAV-mediated gene transfer of alpha7 nAcHRs does not significantly enhance these effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel pharmacological and gene transfer strategies to increase the function of alpha7 nAcChRs in the brain.
the development of new treatments for Alzheimer's disease (AD) and schizophrenia (SZ).
the development of novel pharmacological approaches to the treatment of cognitive impairments associated with Alzheimer's and schizophrenia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alpha7 nAchR activation by 5-Hi or 5-Hi+4OH-Gts-21 is associated with an increase in the number of spontaneous synaptic events.
alpha7 gene transfer does not appear to significantly augment the effects of either alpha7 agonist or alpha7 modulator activation.
alpha7 gene transfer does not appear to be necessary for enhancing the positive effects produced by alpha7 agonists or alpha7 modulators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alpha7 nAchRs are not the only nAchRs involved in the modulation of spontaneous synaptic events, but that alpha7 nachrs do have an important role in the modulation of synaptic transmission.
alpha7 gene transfer may not be a necessary component for enhancing alpha7 nAchR function in the hippocampus, but it may be necessary for enhancing alpha7 receptor function in the neocortex.
alpha7 gene transfer may enhance direct measures of alpha nAChR activation, but may not significantly enhance indirect measures of alpha nACR function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of alpha7 agonist activation and positive allosteric modulators of alpha7 nACHRs may be a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of cognitive deficits associated with Alzheimer's and schizophrenia.
combining alpha7 gene therapy and alpha7 agonism/positive allosteric modulation may not be the optimal strategy for treating cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's disease or schizophrenia.
combining alpha7 gene therapy with either agonist or modulator strategies does not appear to enhance the efficacy of these strategies.
